messages:
maria: Heads-up — we're seeing a latency regression on prod after the CUDA driver push (nodes h100-prod-*) around 03:12 UTC. Affects short sequences (<64 tokens) much worse.

alex_m: saw this in staging earlier, looks like the kernel selection prefers `vec_attn_v2` on these cards now. For our layout that kernel increases launch overhead.

vikram_r: quick profiler summary: kernel launch overhead + serialized small-kernel churn. L2 miss rate up ~18% vs baseline; also noticed KV cache hitrate falling ~6% during warmups.

jen_product: is this a driver ABI change? can we force the runtime to pick the old path while we investigate?

maria: yeah probably a driver/kernel heuristic shift — NV driver changed some occupancy heuristics. We can force a policy override in the autotuner config.

sam_eng: I have a conservative override ready:
```json
{
  "autotune": {
    "kernel_policy": {
      "override": [
        {"seq_max": 64, "prefer": "tiled_attention"},
        {"seq_min": 65, "prefer": "vec_attn_v2"}
      ]
    }
  }
}
```
This pins small sequences to the tiled path. Can push as a canary to 10% of capacity.

kai_perf: perf delta if we apply override (staging numbers): p50 from 12ms->14ms (ok), p95 from 210ms->62ms (huge win), token throughput recovers ~22%. KV cache hit returns to baseline.

maria: thanks. plan: 1) canary override 10% (sam) 2) monitor p95/tail tokens/L2 miss rate/KV hitrate (kai) 3) if canary good, widen to 50% then global. If not, rollback driver.

jen_product: what are the guardrails for aborting canary?

kai_perf: abort if p95 increases >20% over baseline or KV hitrate drops >3% or error rate increases. Also watch p99.

ops-bot: deploy request created by sam_eng: `override-kernel-policy-canary` -> target: h100-prod pool -> 10% traffic. CI checks: OK, config diff small.

sam_eng: rolling canary now. pushing config to 6 nodes.

maria: quick check — any model families more affected? small-chat workloads worst, rerankers ok.

alex_m: FYI we saw similar on one customer on Dedicated — reaching out to account team to alert and offer temporary override.

kai_perf: canary results after 5m: 5/6 nodes passed latency guardrails. Average p95 on canary group dropped from 195ms->63ms. KV hitrate restored.

ops-bot: canary deploy `override-kernel-policy-canary` status: partial-success (5/6). No crashes.

vikram_r: node 3 had higher swap activity during canary, file ticket to look at driver logs: `D-1978882461-DRIVER-LOGS`

maria: next steps: widen canary to 50% for 15m, if stable do global rollout of policy override. Simultaneously open driver rollback plan with infra in case this surfaces other regressions.

jen_product: add note to incident tracker and notify sales for impacted accounts.

sam_eng: widening now. will post final after 15m.

ops-bot: deployment update: widened to 50% -> 18/24 nodes updated.

kai_perf: at 50% steady-state (10m): p95 overall back to baseline, throughput within 5%, no error rate increase. Recommend keep override until NV releases micro update or we adapt kernel heuristics in runtime.

maria: agreed. I'll draft rollback + long-term action: 1) add explicit kernel-selection tests to CI (seq buckets 1/8/32/128) 2) add kernel-policy override knob per model family 3) work with NV on heuristic diff.

alex_m: thanks all. filing follow-ups: #1 runtime autotuner unit tests, #2 perf regression post-driver checklist, #3 dedicated customer reachouts.

ops-bot: status: `override-kernel-policy` rolled out to 100% with config tag `canary-1978882461-override` at 04:02 UTC. No critical alerts.

maria: closing note: keep an eye on small-seq suites for the next 48h. If anything flares, revert override (sam). :thumbsup:
